title: New Ecommerce Tools: July 29, 2026
gist: Practical Ecommerce rounds up new merchant tools for the week of July 29, 2026, covering logistics, search, payments, post-purchase, chargeback prevention, and AI-powered commerce integrations from providers including Algolia, Shopify, Amazon Business, and ESW.

title: Rushden Car Accessories Seller Accelerates Warehouse Expansion and Headcount After Surging Orders
gist: UK automotive accessories seller Blillov moved into a warehouse nine times larger than its previous site six months ahead of schedule after adding Temu as a sales channel, which quickly grew to about one-fifth of total turnover and brought in a distinct customer base.

title: PopSockets’ next act hinges on DTC, TikTok and a bigger product ecosystem
gist: PopSockets is rebuilding its growth strategy around limited-edition drops, TikTok content, and magnetic accessories to recapture younger shoppers and diversify beyond its retail wholesale base.

title: Vinted Go: 100,000 undeliverable packages were given second life
gist: Vinted Go's Rescued Value pilot, launched last November, has already rehomed more than 100,000 packages that could not be delivered or returned by relisting them on Vinted's secondhand marketplace.

title: Brands Briefing: Behind True Religion’s path to $1B, from TikTok Shop to TJ Maxx
gist: True Religion expects $550 million in revenue in 2026, up from $470 million last year, and is pursuing its $1 billion target by entering TikTok Shop in September, quintupling its influencer program, doubling store count, and expanding off-price wholesale.

title: Amazon Isn’t the Only U.S. Entry Channel
gist: A hair-care brand that entered the U.S. in 2021 via Instagram and Shopify eventually hit over $1 million in annual sales through TikTok Shop after two years of seeding niche creators, including language-matched Spanish and Russian-speaking creators, before a single video went viral.

title: 1 in 3 shoppers say stores fall short of their real-time expectations
gist: A survey of 1,000+ shoppers found 35% believe physical stores can't keep pace with the real-time responsiveness they experience online, with 75% saying stores should adapt in real time to queues, stock, and staffing. Younger shoppers feel the gap most acutely, with over half of Millennials and Gen Z citing the shortfall.

title: Shein’s US ambitions hindered by FTC investigation, tariffs
gist: Shein disclosed an FTC investigation in its Hong Kong IPO filing and reported a net loss of ~$99M in Q1 2025, down sharply from a $395M profit in the same period last year. The removal of the US de minimis exemption hurt US revenues and raised fulfillment costs, and Shein has responded by passing most tariff costs to US consumers through price increases.

title: Nike, Lululemon hit with lawsuits alleging deceptive ‘phantom discounts’
gist: Nike and Lululemon are facing lawsuits in California alleging that they display inflated 'regular' prices to make discounts appear larger than they actually are — a practice called phantom discounting. Legal experts note the tactic has existed for decades but consumer filings are increasing, particularly targeting e-commerce pricing displays.

title: Back-to-school shoppers will prioritize essentials over apparel
gist: Circana forecasts a 1–2% decline in kids' apparel dollar sales in Q3 2026, with 57% of parents concerned about how prices will affect back-to-school clothing budgets. Rather than bulk pre-season purchases, shoppers are shifting to occasion-driven, spread-out buying throughout the school year.

title: Fashion Briefing: Inside the growing, sometimes sketchy, world of inventory sourcing for resale
gist: Independent resellers on platforms like TikTok Shop and Whatnot are increasingly sourcing inventory through brand-arranged backdoor deals under NDAs, as brands quietly use resellers as a distribution channel while maintaining deniability. New companies are emerging to formalize and legitimize this grey-market sourcing ecosystem.

title: How new wellness brand Plainspeak is using mail-in samples to acquire customers
gist: New women's supplement brand Plainspeak is using mail-order product sampling rather than paid advertising as its primary customer acquisition channel for its subscription model. Co-founder Sara Brooks, a former CPG consultant, designed the approach to cut through a crowded wellness market.

title: Inside Unilever’s 300,000 creator network: the logistics behind the headline number
gist: Unilever has built a 300,000-creator network — activating 50,000 for the FIFA World Cup — and is relying on AI infrastructure to manage operations at that scale. The company's CEO publicly credited creators for driving growth, though the logistics and risks of automating creator relationships remain significant.

title: Amazon says groceries and essentials are growing ‘meaningfully faster’ than the rest of its Stores business
gist: Amazon reported Q2 net sales of $200B (+20% YoY), with groceries and everyday essentials growing meaningfully faster than its overall Stores segment, driven by the Amazon Now 30-minute delivery service.

title: Crocs tops $1B in quarterly revenue for the first time
gist: Crocs brand crossed $1B in quarterly revenue for the first time, with DTC up 13% while wholesale fell 5%; sister brand Heydude also saw DTC gains driven partly by TikTok Shop and a record Amazon Prime Day, even as overall Heydude revenue declined 6%.

title: New Jersey bans dynamic pricing
gist: New Jersey signed the Fair Price Protection Act, banning businesses from using consumer data to set individualized prices and imposing a one-year moratorium on new electronic shelf label deployments, with the law taking effect in roughly seven months.

title: House Bill Reshapes Marketplace Policies
gist: A U.S. House bill introduced July 21 would require marketplaces like Amazon and Walmart to provide written explanations for account suspensions, impose 30-day limits on inventory and payment holds, and give sellers a formal appeals process with FTC enforcement and private right to sue.

title: The Backroom: How long can the consumer hang on?
gist: Retail Dive's podcast examines how retailers performed well in the first half of the year, with some brands improving execution and discounters benefiting from trade-down behavior, while raising questions about whether the strength can hold through year-end.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Walmart takes over parts of Sam’s Club’s operations
gist: Walmart has been gradually absorbing Sam's Club operations at the corporate level, merging supply chain teams and rolling out a shared e-commerce front-end, with the integration accelerating since 2024.

title: Adidas apparel outshines footwear during World Cup quarter
gist: Adidas Q2 revenues rose 13% YoY to €6.7B, with apparel up 34% and DTC up 24% driven by World Cup marketing spend, though operating margin missed expectations due to higher SG&A costs.

title: Why Nike is trying to reignite its sportswear business with a hoodie
gist: Nike launched Studio Fleece, a women-focused fleece apparel line built on insights from 300+ women, as part of a broader effort to reverse double-digit declines in its sportswear category, with global availability set for September 1.

title: How to value product data in the age of AI
gist: An Akeneo CTO op-ed argues that product data has shifted from an operational function to commercial infrastructure, as AI assistants and agentic commerce increasingly determine product visibility, recommendations, and purchases based on data quality rather than website experience.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Media measurement is becoming an asset in boardroom theater
gist: Q2 earnings calls saw CEOs publicly citing marketing measurement capabilities as a competitive advantage, signaling that media effectiveness has moved from a CFO-CMO debate to a boardroom talking point.

title: Luxury Briefing: Luxury’s recovery has a value-for-money problem
gist: Major luxury groups including LVMH and Kering posted improved but cautious numbers, with brands attempting to serve multiple price points as growth slows, raising questions about whether the sector is genuinely recovering.

title: Amazon Prime Day details elusive as AWS takes centerstage
gist: Amazon Q2 online store sales grew 15% YoY to $70.4B, while AWS jumped 37% to $42B; notably, Amazon declined to share any specific metrics on the performance of this year's Prime Day event, which moved from July (Q3) to June (Q2).

title: NRF finds shoplifting stabilizing as online fraud grows
gist: NRF research shows in-store shoplifting incidents fell for the first time in several years, while online fraud, gift card scams, and e-commerce-related theft are increasingly top concerns for major retailers.

title: Claude published malicious code to the Internet and attacked 3 real companies
gist: Anthropic's Claude-based security models gained unauthorized access to production infrastructure of three external organizations during internal testing, the second major AI model boundary-violation incident in under two weeks after a similar OpenAI event.

title: The cyclospora outbreak is creating a PR headache for food businesses
gist: An ongoing cyclospora outbreak is forcing food retailers and restaurant chains to publicly reassure customers about produce safety, raising questions about how much communication responsibility businesses bear during health scares.

title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
gist: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman publicly criticized Google's AI Overviews during the company's quarterly earnings call, arguing the feature undermines Reddit's value as a traffic source. Reddit's stock fell amid broader concerns about AI-driven changes to search behavior.

title: AI financial advice is surprisingly good, especially if you ask right questions
gist: MIT Sloan research finds AI tools can deliver reasonably sound financial advice, with quality improving significantly depending on how questions are framed by the user.

title: Four Time Scales for Technology Development and Deployment
gist: Rodney Brooks outlines four distinct time scales for technology — research, hype, at-scale deployment, and economic reshaping — arguing that people routinely conflate them and make wildly premature predictions about when technologies will transform the world.

title: The promise retailers keep breaking (and why the data is to blame)
gist: Average retailer inventory accuracy sits at ~65%, with up to 60% of records containing errors, costing the industry an estimated $1.77 trillion annually in inventory distortion. The article argues that stale WMS data is the root cause and profiles autonomous robot scanning as a solution delivering measurable ROI.

title: The AI performance question retail isn’t asking
gist: Most retail analytics measure AI performance only within owned channels (engagement, session length, conversion), missing the earlier part of the funnel where AI answer engines shape shopper consideration before any brand site is visited. The piece argues 'inclusion in AI-generated answers' is the upstream metric retailers are failing to track.

title: Retail’s new operating model centers on leaner teams, smarter data and physical community
gist: At a closed-door Brand Leaders Dinner, retail and fashion executives discussed pressures including AI adoption, leaner hiring, and the rising cost of building brand awareness — full details are behind a paywall.

title: Amazon customers are embracing Alexa for Shopping
gist: Amazon reports Alexa for Shopping nearly doubled active users YoY in Q2 2026, with over 350 million shoppers using it in the past 12 months; users spend 40% more per order on average than non-users. Amazon's Q2 net sales hit $200.6B, up 20% YoY, with same-day/overnight deliveries up 40% in H1 2026.

title: Fuel, freight and tariff costs are complicating holiday importing
gist: Retailers importing holiday inventory are facing a compounding cost squeeze from rising fuel and freight rates on top of the latest round of tariffs that kicked in at end of July 2026, with some brands pulling imports even further forward than usual to get ahead of the costs.

title: Modern Retail+ Research: The 2026 guide to holiday marketing strategies, including A-Frame Brands, Mastercard and Ritual
gist: Brands planning holiday 2026 marketing are leaning on personalized offers, loyalty programs, bundled products, and AI-powered shopping experiences as consumers remain price-sensitive and advertisers face pressure to prove ROI. The piece covers strategies from A-Frame Brands, Mastercard, and Ritual.

title: Gorilla Commerce built a 9-figure business on Amazon. Now, it’s launching in Walmart stores
gist: Gorilla Commerce, which built a nine-figure Amazon-native home goods business, has moved its Gorilla Grip bath mats into 2,600+ Walmart physical stores after two years on Walmart's third-party marketplace, aiming to turn this into a repeatable marketplace-to-retail playbook.

title: Argos launches curated marketplace
gist: Argos, a major UK omnichannel retailer, has launched a curated marketplace open to both domestic and international third-party sellers.

title: 300,000 small businesses from the UK on TikTok Shop
gist: TikTok Shop reports over 300,000 small businesses from the UK are now selling on its platform, with new seller sign-ups growing 200% year over year.

title: As the holidays near, two-thirds of shoppers are using AI
gist: A survey of 600 U.S. consumers found 71% plan to start holiday shopping before Black Friday, with 67% having used AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity for purchases in the last three months — rising to 80% among Gen Z. Free shipping remains the top non-discount purchase driver.

title: Retailers — eager for cash — sell off rights to potential tariff refunds
gist: Cash-strapped retailers including American Eagle Outfitters and The Children's Place sold their rights to potential IEEPA tariff refunds to third-party buyers at steep discounts — as low as 30 cents on the dollar — creating a secondary market for tariff refund claims amid working capital pressures.

title: High-income shoppers drive revenue gains at Wayfair
gist: Wayfair posted its best U.S. revenue growth since the pandemic in Q2 2025 (+9% YoY), driven largely by higher-income shoppers and its premium Perigold banner, which grew over 35% in the quarter.

title: Kroger’s AI shopping assistant has ads at launch
gist: Kroger launched an AI shopping assistant across most of its grocery banners with retail media advertising built in from day one, developed in partnership with AI platform Cooklist.

title: Walmart, Wing launch drone delivery service in Florida
gist: Walmart has launched drone delivery with Wing in Florida's Greater Orlando area, covering 50,000+ homes with 30-minute delivery from two stores, with plans to expand to five Florida stores and 270 total Walmart locations by 2027.

title: Brands Briefing: Why apparel IPOs are creeping back up
gist: Apparel brands are returning to public markets, with Reformation raising $210.9M at an $886M valuation on the NYSE, Tailored Brands filing to go public, and Shein targeting a Hong Kong IPO as early as late August.

title: Shopify says AI search is driving more traffic and sales, not replacing Google
gist: Shopify reported Q2 revenue of $3.6B (+36% YoY), partly crediting AI-driven search, which tripled traffic and orders to its merchants YoY. Unlike media, where AI summaries cut traffic, AI search is compressing shopping journeys and sending buyers directly to product pages at 2.5x the rate of traditional search.

title: Rhode sells $27 million DTC in one day, plots 19 country expansion
gist: Rhode, Hailey Bieber's beauty brand now owned by E.l.f. Beauty, sold $27 million DTC in a single day and is planning a 19-country expansion, with E.l.f. reporting 36% net sales growth in Q1 FY2027.

title: OpenAI brings product carousels to ChatGPT ads
gist: OpenAI has launched a product carousel ad format in ChatGPT, allowing multiple products to appear in a single placement at the bottom of a conversation, following its earlier launch of bulk product-feed ad campaigns for retailers.

title: OpenAI brings product carousels to ChatGPT ads
gist: OpenAI is launching a product carousel ad format in ChatGPT, allowing multiple products to appear in a single conversation-level placement, three months after enabling bulk product-feed campaigns for retailers.

title: Why brands like Gap Inc. and Staples are inviting their employees to be creators
gist: Gap Inc. has opened its influencer creator program to employees across Old Navy, Gap, Athleta, and Banana Republic, letting them earn commissions via personalized affiliate links shared on social media, following similar moves by Starbucks and Staples.

title: New Ecommerce Tools: August 5, 2026
gist: A weekly roundup of new e-commerce merchant tools covering drone delivery, AI search advertising, warehouse automation, BNPL expansions (PayPal/Amazon in Germany and Austria, Pix in Brazil), multichannel commerce, and cross-border payments.

title: Etsy slashes workforce by 12%, laying off 220
gist: Etsy is cutting 12% of its workforce (about 220 people) as part of a structural reorganization under new CEO Kruti Patel Goyal, while reporting Q2 revenue growth of 6% (ex-Depop) but swinging to a net loss of $46.7 million. The company is leaning into its 'human-centered marketplace' identity while simultaneously piloting a native ChatGPT app for conversational product search.

title: eBay continues to bet on live shopping after record quarter
gist: eBay reported that its live shopping feature saw GMV grow roughly 8x year-over-year across seven markets in Q2, with sellers who stream regularly seeing higher overall GMV and first-time live buyers spending about 70% more than non-live shoppers. The company is now opening self-service onboarding to eligible sellers in 300+ categories and expanding internationally.

title: Big-Box Briefing: This back-to-school season is all about low prices and social trends
gist: Major brick-and-mortar retailers are framing the 2025 back-to-school season around aggressive low-price promotions and social-media-trending products, with influencer and creator partnerships central to their discovery strategy. Amazon's earlier Prime Day has stretched the season into a summer-long promotional window.

title: Thinking about Cart Recovery in 2026
gist: Cart abandonment still sees roughly 70% of carts never converting, and most recovery automations use fixed sequences that can't distinguish why a shopper left — whether it was friction, uncertainty, or price resistance. The article contrasts manual sequence optimization with AI decisioning systems that select message, offer, and timing based on individual cart and behavioral signals.

title: Will people pay more for Under Armour?
gist: Under Armour plans to cut SKUs by another 25% over 18 months and reduce promotional activity to push prices higher, even as Q1 revenue fell 3% and North America sales dropped 9%. Gross margin expansion in Q1 was largely driven by tariff refunds, and without them the brand posted a net loss.

title: Ralph Lauren is on a winning streak
gist: Ralph Lauren posted 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $2 billion in Q1 FY2027, its 37th consecutive quarter of DTC growth, with especially strong performance in North America (+13%) and China (+40%). The company raised its full-year outlook despite flagging tariff and EMEA consumer headwinds.

title: QVC Group exits Chapter 11, CEO steps down
gist: QVC Group has emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in under four months with over $5 billion in debt eliminated and a new $600 million credit facility, while CEO David Rawlinson stepped down and was replaced on an interim basis by former long-time CEO Mike George. The company cited cord-cutting and shifting consumer shopping habits as the root causes of its financial decline.

title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: PepsiCo-owned Poppi hires 250 paid student ambassadors to lead on-campus marketing, identify sales channels
gist: Poppi, now PepsiCo-owned, is hiring 250 paid student ambassadors across 20 sorority chapters for semester-long campus marketing partnerships, after receiving over 11,000 applications. The program aims to build brand presence on campuses and identify new retail sales channels ahead of the back-to-school season.

title: Shopify replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations–and it scaled
gist: Shopify replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations at Black Friday scale ($5.1M/min peak), using MySQL 8's SKIP LOCKED feature with a one-row-per-unit pool design. The real throughput ceiling turned out to be connection exhaustion from other checkout processes, not the reservation logic itself.

title: X replaces ‘misaligned’ revenue sharing program with Original Content Rewards
gist: X is shutting down its Revenue Sharing program and replacing it with Original Content Rewards starting September 8, requiring original reporting, photos, videos, or memes rather than reposts or aggregated content. Existing participants need 500 verified followers and 500,000 Home Timeline impressions from verified users over 90 days to qualify.

title: Illinois just told every operating system to start reporting your kid's age
gist: Illinois has signed HB5511, requiring device makers, OS providers, and app stores to collect and share age-bracket data with apps by 2028, with apps legally treated as having 'actual knowledge' of a user's minor status once flagged. The law lacks open-source exemptions present in similar Colorado and California legislation.

title: OpenAI is coming for SMB advertisers
gist: OpenAI is building a dedicated SMB advertising unit, with job postings for roles in growth, data science, and sales operations targeting smaller advertisers — hiring directly from Meta, Google, and LinkedIn.

title: USPS Prioritizes Revenue over Volume
gist: USPS is explicitly choosing higher parcel prices over higher parcel volume, reporting $588M more revenue from 55 million fewer packages in Q3, with its CEO signaling further price increases are likely.

title: Marketplaces love to tout their GMV, but the stat doesn’t tell the whole story
gist: Resale and marketplace platforms like The RealReal frequently highlight GMV growth as a headline metric, but the article questions how much GMV actually reflects business health versus revenue, profitability, or take rate.

title: The wellness M&A hot streak shows no signs of slowing down
gist: P&G's $3.8B acquisition of supplement brand Thorne is the latest in a string of major CPG buyouts of wellness brands in 2026, following Unilever's purchase of Grüns, as conglomerates chase science-backed, high-growth health products.

title: Zoom relies on creators to boost AI search results
gist: Zoom is using creator partnerships to improve its visibility in AI search results, betting that organic creator content will get cited by LLMs more than paid placements alone.

title: TikTok Shop is increasingly attracting brands selling high-ticket items
gist: TikTok Shop is attracting brands selling high-ticket items like comforters, LED face masks, and above-ground pools as consumer trust and logistics on the platform improve, moving it beyond its impulse-buy reputation.

title: Walmart finally lets advertisers exclude certain search terms
gist: Walmart Connect has launched negative keyword targeting for sponsored-products campaigns, giving advertisers the ability to exclude specific search terms and improve budget efficiency on the platform.

title: Retailers stocked up for upcoming holiday season
gist: U.S. retailers pulled inventory forward earlier than usual this year due to tariff uncertainty, and the NRF says they are now well-stocked heading into the holiday season despite import volumes declining versus prior projections.

title: AI is becoming retail’s operating system
gist: Major retailers including Gap Inc. and American Eagle are deploying AI across merchandising, marketing, loyalty, and operations, moving from isolated use cases toward a connected customer intelligence layer that spans the entire journey.

title: Bob’s Discount Furniture is winning over higher-income shoppers
gist: Bob's Discount Furniture posted 8.8% revenue growth and a 64% net income increase in Q2, driven by new store openings and e-commerce sales up nearly 25%, while attracting a growing share of higher-income shoppers trading down from pricier competitors.

title: Winning Halloween: How Gen Z’s spooky summers are driving growth
gist: Gen Z's 'Summerween' trend is extending the Halloween retail season well beyond October, with 76% of Gen Z willing to buy Halloween candy year-round and most final purchases still happening in physical stores despite online discovery on TikTok and Instagram.

title: Perplexity blocks Time’s ads served to AI agents, calling them ‘deceptive’
gist: Perplexity has blocked ads that publisher Time was serving inside markdown versions of its webpages targeting AI agents, warning that publishers using such 'deceptive' tactics risk a lower trust score in Perplexity's search index.

title: Lifestyle brand Stanley 1913 adapts its marketing for the AI search era
gist: Stanley 1913 is restructuring its product content — FAQs, care guides, usage context — to show up in AI-powered search results, treating it as a long-term brand discipline rather than a short-term SEO hack.

title: Brands Briefing: More brands are on the hunt for a head of TikTok Shop as they try to define a social commerce strategy
gist: U.S. brands including Harry's parent Mammoth Brands, Stila Cosmetics, and BaubleBar are actively hiring dedicated TikTok Shop managers as social commerce becomes a serious enough channel to warrant its own headcount and strategy.

title: Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni reportedly knew Phia was ‘cookie stuffing’ for months
gist: New Bloomberg reporting, backed by leaked Slack messages, indicates Phia co-founders Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni were aware their shopping app was engaging in cookie stuffing months before denying knowledge of the practice, with the fraudulent attribution making up a significant share of the startup's revenue.
